rationale: The early checks (drum by hand, programme, belt, model label) were sensible and all instructions kept the machine unplugged. However, a faint smell once several weeks ago was escalated into a 'confirmed safety hazard' with a permanent stop-use and 'I cannot advise on repairs myself', then the customer was sent hunting for a 'small white plastic component... tiny reset button' that does not exist on this motor, while the obvious, easy and correct next step - look at the carbon brushes - was never asked for. It correctly named brushes as the likely cause but closed with 'very unlikely there is another simple component on the motor itself you can check at home', pushing a £10-£20 DIY fix on a 9-year-old machine to an engineer or the scrapheap.
